---
title: "Glossary"
---

Short, precise definitions for terms used across chapters. Each chapter
explains its own core concepts in depth — this page is for the term you half
remember from two chapters ago, not a substitute for reading the chapter.

**Abelian group** — a group whose operation is commutative
($a \ast b = b \ast a$ for all elements). Not required by the group axioms
themselves. See [Groups](chapters/08-groups.qmd).

**Affine combination** — a weighted sum of points whose weights sum to
exactly $1$; unlike an arbitrary sum of points, this is always well-defined.
See [Affine Spaces](chapters/15-affine-spaces.qmd).

**Affine map** — a linear map plus a translation; generalizes a linear map
to a setting with no origin to fix. See [Affine
Spaces](chapters/15-affine-spaces.qmd).

**Affine space** — a set of points, a vector space of displacements, and an
action translating points by displacements, such that any two points
determine a unique displacement. Formalizes "points don't add, but their
difference is a vector." See [Affine Spaces](chapters/15-affine-spaces.qmd).

**Axiom** — a starting statement accepted without proof, from which theorems
are derived. Not "true" in isolation — true relative to the choice of
axioms. See [Axioms and Definitions](chapters/05-axioms-and-definitions.qmd).

**Basis** — a linearly independent set of vectors that spans a vector space;
every vector is then a unique linear combination of basis vectors. See
[Vector Spaces](chapters/09-vector-spaces.qmd).

**Bijective** — both injective and surjective; pairs two sets up perfectly,
element for element. See [Relations and
Functions](chapters/04-relations-and-functions.qmd).

**Completeness** — a metric space's property that every Cauchy sequence
(one whose terms bunch arbitrarily close together) actually converges to a
point in the space. $\mathbb{R}$ has it; $\mathbb{Q}$ doesn't. See [Metric
Spaces](chapters/12-metric-spaces.qmd).

**Continuous** — classically, the $\varepsilon$–$\delta$ definition;
topologically, a function whose preimage of every open set is open — the
same idea, restated without needing a distance. See [Topological
Spaces](chapters/13-topological-spaces.qmd).

**Dimension** — the number of vectors in a basis of a vector space; the same
for every basis of a given space. See [Vector
Spaces](chapters/09-vector-spaces.qmd).

**Eigenvalue / eigenvector** — a nonzero vector $v$ that a linear map $T$
only stretches or shrinks ($T(v) = \lambda v$), never redirects, and the
scalar $\lambda$ by which it does so. See [Linear
Algebra](chapters/10-linear-algebra.qmd).

**Equivalence relation** — a relation that is reflexive, symmetric, and
transitive; partitions a set into equivalence classes. Used to construct
$\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{Q}$ from more primitive number systems. See
[Relations and Functions](chapters/04-relations-and-functions.qmd) and
[Number Systems](chapters/06-number-systems.qmd).

**Euclidean space** — an affine space whose vector space of displacements
carries an inner product; the modern, coordinate-based redefinition of the
geometry Euclid built from postulates. See [Euclidean
Geometry](chapters/16-euclidean-geometry.qmd).

**Field** — a ring in which multiplication is commutative and every nonzero
element has a multiplicative inverse; the scalars a vector space is defined
"over." $\mathbb{Q}$, $\mathbb{R}$, $\mathbb{C}$ are fields, $\mathbb{Z}$ is
not. See [Rings and Fields](chapters/11-rings-and-fields.qmd).

**Function** — a relation $f \subseteq A \times B$ in which every element of
$A$ appears as the first coordinate of exactly one pair. See [Relations and
Functions](chapters/04-relations-and-functions.qmd).

**Group** — a set with one operation satisfying closure, associativity,
identity, and inverses. See [Groups](chapters/08-groups.qmd).

**Homomorphism** — a map between two structures of the same kind that
respects their operations; need not be invertible. See [What Is a
Mathematical Structure?](chapters/07-mathematical-structures.qmd).

**Injective** — a function under which distinct inputs always give distinct
outputs ("one-to-one"). See [Relations and
Functions](chapters/04-relations-and-functions.qmd).

**Inner product** — a symmetric, linear, positive-definite function
$\langle u,v\rangle$ on a vector space; induces a norm ($\|v\| =
\sqrt{\langle v,v\rangle}$) and an angle between vectors. See [Inner
Product Spaces](chapters/14-inner-product-spaces.qmd).

**Isomorphism** — an invertible homomorphism; identifies two structures as
"the same" up to relabeling their elements. See [What Is a Mathematical
Structure?](chapters/07-mathematical-structures.qmd).

**Linear combination** — $c_1 v_1 + \cdots + c_k v_k$, for scalars $c_i$ and
vectors $v_i$. See [Vector Spaces](chapters/09-vector-spaces.qmd).

**Linear map** — a function $T: V \to W$ between vector spaces satisfying
$T(u+v) = T(u)+T(v)$ and $T(cv) = cT(v)$. A matrix is what a linear map
looks like once bases are fixed. See [Linear
Algebra](chapters/10-linear-algebra.qmd).

**Manifold** — informally, a topological space that locally resembles
$\mathbb{R}^n$ near every point, even if it doesn't globally (a sphere's
surface is the standard example). A first pass only — full treatment is a
later phase of this site. See [Euclidean
Geometry](chapters/16-euclidean-geometry.qmd).

**Mathematical structure** — a set equipped with operations and/or relations
satisfying a fixed list of axioms — e.g. group, vector space, metric space.
See [What Is a Mathematical
Structure?](chapters/07-mathematical-structures.qmd).

**Metric / metric space** — a function $d(x,y)$ measuring distance between
points of a set, satisfying identity of indiscernibles, symmetry, and the
triangle inequality; the set plus that function is a metric space. See
[Metric Spaces](chapters/12-metric-spaces.qmd).

**Norm** — a length function $\|v\|$ on a vector space; every inner product
induces one, but not every norm comes from an inner product (test: the
parallelogram law). See [Inner Product
Spaces](chapters/14-inner-product-spaces.qmd).

**Open set** — in a metric space, a set where every point has some room
around it (an open ball) still inside the set; in a topological space, a
member of the designated collection $\tau$ that defines the topology. See
[Metric Spaces](chapters/12-metric-spaces.qmd) and [Topological
Spaces](chapters/13-topological-spaces.qmd).

**Orthogonal** — two vectors $u,v$ with $\langle u,v\rangle = 0$; the
structural definition behind "perpendicular." See [Inner Product
Spaces](chapters/14-inner-product-spaces.qmd).

**Proof** — a finite chain of statements, each an axiom or a valid
consequence of earlier statements, ending at the claim being established.
See [Logic and Proof](chapters/02-logic-and-proof.qmd).

**Proposition** — a statement that is unambiguously true or false. See
[Logic and Proof](chapters/02-logic-and-proof.qmd).

**Relation** — a subset of a Cartesian product $A \times B$; the general
notion underlying equality, order, divisibility, and functions alike. See
[Relations and Functions](chapters/04-relations-and-functions.qmd).

**Ring** — a set with two operations, $+$ and $\times$, where $(R,+)$ is an
abelian group, $\times$ is associative, and $\times$ distributes over $+$.
$\mathbb{Z}$ and the $n \times n$ matrices are rings that aren't fields. See
[Rings and Fields](chapters/11-rings-and-fields.qmd).

**Set** — a collection of distinct objects, unordered, without repetition.
See [Sets](chapters/03-sets.qmd).

**Span** — the set of all linear combinations of a given collection of
vectors. See [Vector Spaces](chapters/09-vector-spaces.qmd).

**Surjective** — a function whose range is its entire codomain ("onto").
See [Relations and Functions](chapters/04-relations-and-functions.qmd).

**Theorem** — a statement derivable from a theory's axioms by valid
inference. See [Axioms and Definitions](chapters/05-axioms-and-definitions.qmd).

**Topological space** — a set with a designated collection of subsets
("open sets") closed under arbitrary unions and finite intersections,
including the whole set and the empty set. Every metric space is one; not
every topological space comes from a metric. See [Topological
Spaces](chapters/13-topological-spaces.qmd).

**Vector space** — a set with addition and scalar multiplication satisfying
eight axioms; instances include $\mathbb{R}^n$, polynomials, matrices, and
function spaces. See [Vector Spaces](chapters/09-vector-spaces.qmd).

**Zero divisor** — a nonzero element $a$ of a ring for which some other
nonzero $b$ satisfies $ab=0$. Can't happen in a field; happens routinely
among matrices. See [Rings and Fields](chapters/11-rings-and-fields.qmd).
